title: Tools, extracted (folio-assistant-core)
description: Candidate terms extracted from every Tool node: `title` as the label, `description` as the definition, the Tool id as the code. Generated by folio-assistant-core/scripts/glossary-extract.ts; not curated, and never hand-edited: a person promotes a term by authoring it in a glossary of their own.

terms.definition: Make an ArchiMate model agree with the instance's folio-glossary/v1 terms whose `focus` is an ArchiMate element: elements matched by their `skosConcept` property (never by name) take the term's prefLabel and definition, a term with no element gets one on no view, and the relationships the terms list are added. A type that disagrees is reported, never changed. A relationship between two linked elements that no term lists is reported, and removed with `--prune` along with the lines that draw it. No box or line is moved. Without `--write` it only reports; `--check` fails when anything would change. `--seed` goes the other way once, and only from an ingested model held under `library/` (`--from`): an authored model is never a source of the glossary.

Render every reference in the checkout (each declared `references` directory's folio-reference/v1 nodes and each `catalogue` directory's Dublin Core records) as the bibliography page and one page per sub-graph, each with its BibTeX, CSL-JSON, RIS and Dublin Core JSON-LD exports and a per-reference export, at the route of the visualiser core declares for it.

Each labelled block's links back to where it can be changed: [edit] opens the block's Markdown source in GitHub's editor on `main`, and [feedback] opens a new GitHub issue about the block, from the folio's `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/block-feedback.yml` when it has one (prefilling only the fields it declares: block, section, source, page, url) or as a plain issue whose body carries the same facts. The document build draws these on every block; this Tool prints them as JSON for one block or all. Governed by the `block-actions` skill.

terms.prefLabel: Catalogue a library from its bibliography
terms.definition: Write one `folio-dublin-core/v1` record and one `folio-catalogue-node/v1` item per library entry that the source ledger joins to a CSL-JSON reference, into the folio's declared `catalogue` directory, so `gen-library-jsonld` reads the title from the catalogue's `dc.title` instead of falling to the PDF or the slug. The join is exact: a ledger row naming the entry's `structure.json` source file, one reference id, and the same sha256 where both record one. Unjoined entries are reported and left alone. Never touches a node it did not write.

terms.prefLabel: Verify Data Sharing Agreement hash, citation, and vocabulary terms
terms.definition: Verify a Data Sharing Agreement (DSA) directory or single version: checks that every JSON-LD term in `agreement.jsonld` and `dcat.jsonld` is defined in the SHA-256-pinned official W3C ODRL 2.2, W3C DCAT 3 (with SPDX 2.2.2 and ADMS), or DCMI Metadata Terms contexts; checks that the ODRL 2.2 Agreement's `uid` is the version's fixed-version URL and its `dcterms:source` cites the DCAT 3 `dcat:Distribution` whose `spdx:checksum` is checked; verifies that the SHA-256 digest of `agreement.md` matches `spdx:checksumValue`; and checks `dcat:previousVersion` and hash distinctness across versions.

terms.prefLabel: DIIG phases, steps and resources chart
terms.definition: Draw a DIIG "phases, steps and resources" chart as SVG from `diig-phases-figure/v1` data on a who-iris library entry (DIIG Fig. 1.1.1, or a handbook's republished version such as the product catalogue handbook's Fig. 4), or from a folio's `diig-phases-adaptation/v1` file that adds its own tiles and marks itself "(this document)". Every label comes from the data; tiles link to their library entry or glossary concept.

Render every `folio-dublin-core/v1` record a catalogue item names as Dublin Core XML (qualified DC, per DCMI's XML guidelines) and as JSON-LD bound to DCMI Metadata Terms. Both are written into the instance's published root (`<instanceRoot>/dublin-core/<stem>.dc.xml` and `.dc.jsonld`), so the site mount publishes them beside the item pages. Deterministic. `--check` fails on a missing, stale or orphaned rendering. Governed by the `dublin-core-renderings` skill.

For every figure a source publication declares, report whether the folio built from it has a block and how computable it is: missing, excluded (signed off), picture (a PNG crop), linked (a picture linked to a model view), computable (a diagram, a table or a figure rebuilt by ArchiMate, BPMN, DMN, Mermaid, a class diagram or a generator), or cited (a picture kept on purpose, signed off). Exits non-zero when any declared figure is missing; `--require-computable` also fails on pictures, linked or not.

Summarise a folio's committed per-block QA verdicts into one `block-qa.json` a staging preview publishes: each block is failing (a FRESH verdict failed, with the worst severity), stale (a verdict predates the block's current files), passing, or unaudited. Freshness is the QA sweep's own rule, including the uses-graph hash for graph-scoped criteria. Runs no checker and writes no verdict.

Picture each changed figure, diagram, table, equation or simulator block on the published main site and on a staging build, and compare the two pictures pixel by pixel in Chromium's canvas. Writes `visual-diff.json` (`folio-visual-diff/v1`: per block, the share of pixels changed beyond anti-aliasing, and the before, after and diff pictures) and `visual/*.png`, which the review page's visual renderer shows. A side that cannot be pictured (page or anchor missing) is recorded as missing, never drawn blank. Drives Chromium through Playwright.

What changed in a folio between two git refs, block by block: each block added, removed, or changed — and for a changed block, every aspect that applies (renamed, prose, manifest, moved). Keyed on the block label, which the `id-unique` / `id-stable` QA criteria guard, not on file paths.

A review-process task moves one `review-comment/1.0.0` todo's status (address, send back, resolve, adjudicate, withdraw) through `transition()`, which refuses any move the named BPMN task may not make. The comment is written to the folio's todos graph (its declared `todo-feedback` directory) and, with `--commit`, committed to the edit-set's FEATURE branch. Refused on the base branch and on a detached HEAD.

Ingest a pull request's tagged conversation comments (`block: <label>` on the first line) into `review-comment/1.0.0` todos, and write them as `review-comments.json`. Idempotent over its previous output, whose statuses it keeps. Re-anchors every comment against the head's blocks, following `renamedFrom`, and orphans a comment whose block is gone rather than dropping it.

Compute the two facts `content-change-review.bpmn`'s coverage gate (`GW_Covered`) reads: `uncoveredBlocks`, the changed blocks with no reviewer verdict on their CURRENT hash, and `openDefects`. Reads a preview's `changeset.json`, `blocks.json` and `review-comments.json`. With `--commit`, writes the ingested `folio-review-verdict/v1` verdicts into the todos graph's declared `review-verdicts` directory and commits them to the edit-set's FEATURE branch; refused on the base branch and a detached HEAD. Prints the facts as JSON on stdout.

Build a paper's glossary index from its manifests and render the LaTeX. `--check` reports drift instead of writing, comparing everything except the `generated` timestamp so a re-run is not mistaken for a change.

Read a source's glossary and abbreviations sections (an L1 entry's sections/, or a folio block) into `candidate` terms of a folio-glossary/v1 scheme, verbatim, each with `source: <file>#L<line>`. Acronyms fold into the term they expand as `notation`. The scheme is merged: terms a person owns are never changed. `--check` writes nothing and fails when the scheme would change.

Render every declared glossary — authored SKOS schemes, the swimlane ledger and the terms extracted from knowledge-graph assets — as the glossary page and one page per asset type, at the route of the visualiser core declares for it.

Rewrite the glossary and acronyms tables of a document from its folio-glossary/v1 schemes, as `glossary/glossary-tables.json` (folio-glossary-tables/v1) lists them: terms with their altLabels, definitions and editorial notes, or acronyms (notation and prefLabel). The block's caption and footnotes are left alone. `--check` writes nothing and fails when a table is stale.

Of the normative sentences in a publication (the closed marker list of the methodology `l1-coverage` §1), count how many an L1 extraction CAPTURED, how many are EXCLUDED for a fixed-list reason a person signed off, and how many are UNACCOUNTED — per page and in total. Writes the contract's §4 report and exits non-zero below 100% accounted-for.

terms.prefLabel: Publish extracted statements with source links
terms.definition: Render each declared page (a `folio-statement-page/v1` spec naming `folio-extracted-statements/v1` lists) as Markdown: every statement extracted from a library source, verbatim, with its kind and status, linked to its library entry and to the section it came from, labelled in the source's own unit ("Catch up schedule, slide 7"). A statement whose source does not resolve fails the run and nothing is written. `--check` fails when a committed page is stale.

Rewrite each reference-list block of a document (a block whose `meta.referenceList` is set) from the folio-reference/v1 nodes its `cites` names, in that order: the node's `printed` text verbatim when it has one, otherwise WHO style (or the short `Authors. Title. Year.` form), as a numbered or bulleted list. The block's `.md` is generated whole. `--check` writes nothing and fails when a list is stale.

terms.prefLabel: Check a review log and its repository's issues for changes
terms.definition: The mechanical check a review-log watcher runs on every poll. Given a drafting sheet's Contributor Feedback values and the folio repository, it reads the repository's open and closed issues (leaving out pull requests, issues labelled `no-sheet` and, with `--author`, issues someone else opened) and compares a digest of them and of the cells people set (Title, Selected Sections, Contributor Feedback, Disposition, Ready for agent, Ready for merge, Dispositions confirmed; on a public-comment log also Committee Feedback, TWG (CS), TWG (human) and Change Set (human)) with the last check's. Unchanged: it prints `{"status":"unchanged"}` and exits 0. Changed: it exits 10 and lists what changed (issue opened, updated or closed; a cell's old and new text), the Contributor Feedback rows to append, one per issue that no row's Issue cell links yet (Title the issue's title, the first Contributor Feedback column `@login (#N): first paragraph`, Issue the issue's URL; a closed issue's row marked `closed`), and `closedRows`, the rows linking a closed issue, which the watcher hides with their text struck through. A read with no Issue column (a public-comment log's Review Change Sets) tracks only issues labelled `change-set` unless `--label` says otherwise, and appends no rows: each open issue is reported as an `issue-unlinked` change instead. It writes no sheet and no issue: the watcher appends the rows and does the agent pass. With `--accept` it stores the new state for the next poll to compare against.

terms.prefLabel: Build the review sheet's Apps Script and a document's Config tab
terms.definition: Builds `Code.gs` (`--script`), the one Google Apps Script every review sheet runs (from `review-sheet.gs`), and one document's Config tab rows (`--config`), filled from the folio's `review/public-comment/sheet-sync.json`, its review anchors and the draft's `pdf-line-map.json`. The script keeps a public-comment review sheet's links and joins current: each comment No. links to its comment page; Sections, Page and Line no(s) link to the page of the frozen review draft; Review Change Sets joins its comments, suggested revisions, feedback and dispositions, each `No. n` linking to its row; and on both tabs Agentic status lists each pull request of the change-set, linked, with its status and what it changed, from the Agent tab. It reads the document's URLs, tab and column names and data from the sheet's Config tab (visible, locked to the owner), which the agent writes from these rows. A person pastes the script (one file) into the sheet once (Extensions > Apps Script) and runs `installTriggers`; from then on the sheet rebuilds itself within about a minute of an edit, with no agent. With `"mode": "drafting"` in the config it builds the drafting sheet instead: one Contributor Feedback tab where each row is a change set (ids assigned by the script), Sections picked from the document's table of contents and linked to it, and Issue and Agentic status from the Agent tab.

Draw the WHO SMART Guidelines approach chart (knowledge layers L1–L5 with their products, and their country adaptations, between the research, localisation and impact bands) as SVG from `smart-guidelines-approach-figure/v1` data on a who-iris library entry, such as the product catalogue handbook's Fig. 5. Every label comes from the data.

Read a delimited text file into a `folio-tabular-csvw/v1` record: one table, its columns and their CSVW datatypes, each measured or explicitly undetermined. Routing is by content, never by extension: the first rows must agree on one field count of two or more, under exactly one of `,` `;` TAB `|`. A CSV's `fac:anchor` sheet and cell are a determined null. Governed by the `tabular-metadata` skill.

Read a workbook into a `folio-tabular-csvw/v1` record, one CSVW table per rectangular block of cells. Blocks are split on empty rows, then on empty columns, so several tables on one sheet are found, each anchored at its real top-left cell (`fac:anchor`: sheet, A1 cell, row, column). Dates are read through the number formats in `styles.xml`, not misread as integer serials. A malformed part is refused rather than half-read. Reads the ZIP with `node:zlib` and SpreadsheetML with `fast-xml-parser`. Governed by the `tabular-metadata` skill.
